## Historical audit — S0164

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C1/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. This audit covers only supplied chunk 1 of 2; the images themselves are not visible here.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 [0,9220); student response, line 3 [0,12224) | The explicit goal was a separate-mesh reconstruction of a single RGB image. The student **inferred** a kitchen with island, extractor, dark cabinets, foreground timber post and ceiling beams; its image bounds and occlusion description are not independent verification of the reference. |
| Student source, lines 3 [0,12224), 6 [0,11973) | The programs specify multiple objects and grouped parts: island body, drawers and countertop; sink and tap; hood, cabinets, ovens, kettle, posts and room. They position parts by coordinates rather than demonstrating physical connections. Colored materials, procedural timber noise and bump are coded; successful assignment and visual appearance are not established by names alone. Objects are static; no articulated pose is evidenced. |
| Harness request, line 4 [0,21752); student response, line 6 [0,11973); execution, lines 7–8 [0,12634), [0,39876) | A pre-execution **source audit** was requested, not a teacher diagnosis. The student changed camera, island dimensions and post position, added a geometric fallback for wood targeting, and stated no render had been inspected. Step 1 reported `ok: true` and saved a render and blend file. |
| Student request and response, lines 11 [0,74330), 13 [0,11790); execution, lines 14–15 [0,12449), [0,40122) | The harness supplied the reference and step 1 render for comparison. The student returned a revised program without the requested explicit discrepancy list: it changed camera, room and hood heights, post position and material handling. Step 2 also reported `ok: true` and saved a render. These are technical successes, not proof of visual agreement. |
| Student response and execution, lines 20 [0,11875), 21 [0,12534) | The student described step 2 cabinets/ceiling as too pale, the island as small and leftward, and the post as misplaced. It proposed and executed step 3 with explicit box-material matching, darker finishes, reduced lighting, a 48 mm lens and changed post/hood placement. These diagnoses are student claims; the supplied excerpt has no step 3 result. |

**Input and exploration.** No separate teacher input, teacher detection or diagnosis appears in this visible portion; consequently there is no evidence of teacher advice being received or adopted. The student performed its own prompted source review and render-driven revisions. Session records report zero tool calls within those model sessions; Blender executions were harness events (lines 2, 5, 12, 19; lines 7, 14, 21). Selection events recorded steps 1 and 2 after their respective results (lines 9–10, 16–17); they do not establish final submission or comparative quality.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Two builds formally executed and rendered; reconstruction correctness and final outcome remain **unknown**. Step 3 was launched, not visibly completed in this chunk. Whether the material-targeting hypothesis fixed pale surfaces, whether parts actually meet, and whether camera, lighting, occlusion and geometry match the photograph remain unresolved without the images or later evidence. A transferable lesson is to distinguish source checks and successful rendering from visual validation; the particular camera, post and shader adjustments are task-specific hypotheses.
